doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Singing T'ain't What You Do at his Tonight Show birthday
summary: Brown mentions a clip of Young singing the Lunceford tune on the Tonight Show; Young says someone arranged it for him.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So, when you left the Tonight Show Band in ‘92, oh let me talk about a film clip that‘s on the internet, it‘s of your birthday party and you have a celebration I think it‘s in 1989 they‘re celebrating I think it must be your 70th birthday. And you come out and you sing, you come out in front of the band and you sing ―T‘aint What You Do It‘s The Way That You Do It‖
Oh, you mean with the Tonight Show?
Yeah. Do you remember that? When you came out front for your birthday?
Yeah, in front of the band. Well, see, that song…
That song was from Lunceford‘s band.

And, what‘s his name wrote an arrangement for me to do, who wrote that arrangement… might have been Tommy Newsom, but he wrote this arrangement, I told him what I wanted to do and everything and ―T‘aint what you do‖ that, they knew I was from Lunceford‘s band, that tune is from Lunceford‘s band. [Sings] ―T‘aint what you do it‘s the way that you do it.‖ [laughs]
